podcast.body: This version of "The Twist" went to number one on the Billboard Pop Chart as a result of Dick Clark's constant plugging on his TV shows. It was so similar to Hank Ballard's original version that Ballard initially believed it was his own record. Key differences included Checker's drummer playing more on the cymbals and his saxophone player playing all the way through the song, rather than just a solo. The record re-entered the charts 18 months after its initial release, returning to number one, making it the only non-Christmas themed record to achieve this feat in American history. As recently as 2018, Billboard listed it as the all-time number one record on the Hot 100. "It was so close to Ballard's version that when Ballard first heard it on the radio, he was convinced it was his own record."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: First Song to Hit #1 in Two Separate Runs
podcast.body: This dance craze, released by Chubby Checker, first climbed to the top of the Hot 100 in September 1960, fueled by teenagers learning the dance from TV's American Bandstand. More than a year later, in 1961, as celebrity photos performing the Twist appeared in newspapers and second-wave twist records emerged, the dance became acceptable for adults. This resurgence caused the 1960 hit to re-enter the Hot 100, climbing back to number one by January 1962. It achieved a historical milestone by becoming the first ever single to reach number one in two separate chart runs. "Chubby Checkers, the twist, became the first ever single to reach number one in two separate chart runs."
